result.title: Same Beliefs, Different Policies: Learning Reusable Representations for Early Stopping in LLM Reasoning
result.summary: Reasoning LLMs often continue reasoning after reaching a correct answer, wasting computation and sometimes replacing it with an incorrect one. Deciding when to stop is a metareasoning problem: the model must weigh what further reasoning could achieve against its cost, given what it can already answer. Direct utility training learns a stopping representation at a chosen token price; supporting new prices can require additional controller training. We introduce BELT (BELief-based Termination), which separates outcome prediction from stopping control. It learns beliefs about current and future answers from a frozen LLM's hidden states, then fits a linear stopping policy on the frozen features. The prediction targets are independent of token price, so one probe supports different accuracy-cost trade-offs through CPU policy refitting or threshold adjustment. Averaged over five out-of-distribution (OOD) math benchmarks, BELT reduces generated tokens by 41% on Qwen3-1.7B and 51% on OLMo-3-7B-Think without loss of accuracy. The same math-trained BELT transfers to coding and agentic tasks without training on code or agentic data. In all three domains, its accuracy-cost trade-offs are competitive with or better than those of end-to-end controllers. On OLMo3, its probe has 21.2x fewer parameters than one checkpoint of the strongest baseline, OS-Pruner, and needs 55x fewer training GPU-hours than OS-Pruner's five price-specific checkpoints.

AI.brief_summary: BELT 将结果预测与停止控制解耦：从冻结 LLM 的隐藏状态学习当前与未来答案的信念，再用线性策略决定何时停止，从而以同一探针支持多种准确率—成本权衡，并跨数学、代码和 agentic 任务迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其冻结隐藏状态上的信念探针与可重拟合停止策略，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 决策、状态读出与计算成本控制；但研究对象是纯文本推理，未涉及视觉证据或 latent 视觉状态生成。
